clue.text: Loose cows on farm creating potentially tricky problem

indicators.note: animals let loose scatter, so the letters of the three words are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cattle escaping on a farm cause a messy situation for the farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' reads as describing the cows but signals that COWS ON FARM is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a situation that, once opened up, unleashes a mass of complications.

clue.text: Caught boat regularly to circle posh island

indicators.note: the outer letters go round, so they surround the letter for posh

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from the word boat, here its first and third

parts.note: U is the crossword letter for upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: Someone is caught taking a boat round a smart island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks BA from boat; 'to circle' puts C and BA around U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean nation is a large island south of Florida.

clue.text: In no case is Italy blocking new anaesthetic

indicators.note: one piece sits within another, obstructing it, so the letter for Italy goes inside the anaesthetic

parts.note: ether was an early general anaesthetic
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A claim that Italy never obstructs a new anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; 'blocking' puts I inside ETHER, after N.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb after a negative, as in 'I don't either', it means not in any case.

clue.text: Employment perk, something a hairdresser might suggest?

definitions.meaning: an extra given to staff besides salary, such as a company car
a playful reading: a hair stylist recommending a cut of bangs over the forehead as an advantage

explanation.surface: A job perk is compared to advice from a hairdresser.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into a front lock of hair and an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-wage advantage provided by an employer, such as health insurance or a pension.

clue.text: Postponed number going around vessel's cargo area

indicators.note: turning round, so the abbreviation for number is read backwards

parts.note: the hold is the space below a ship's deck for cargo

explanation.surface: A number circles the cargo space of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put off or suspended until later is in a state of delay.

clue.text: Second American admitting irregular unit is insubordinate

indicators.note: letting something in, so the moment holds the shuffled letters

parts.note: MO is short for a moment, a second

indicators.note: out of the usual order, so the letters of unit are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American deputy lets in a disorderly unit that refuses orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal but is MO, a moment, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebellious and defiant toward authority, like sailors rising against a captain.

clue.text: Wild animal said to be nuisance

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the animal's name is heard as a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: A wild beast is reputed to be a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome person or thing is an annoyance or tedious pest.

clue.text: Decision affecting lawful position of striker?

definitions.text: Decision affecting lawful position of striker?

parts.words: Decision affecting lawful position of striker?
parts.note: a striker sounds like someone on industrial action, but here is a football forward judged by the referee to be in an illegal position

explanation.surface: A ruling that affects the legal standing of someone on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a worker on strike; in football it is a forward, and this ruling decides whether their position was legal.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, an assistant referee's flag call when an attacker is beyond the last defender.

clue.text: Praising European Union record, good restricting international crime

indicators.note: holding something in, so the letters for international and crime go inside

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
a sin is a wrongdoing or offence

explanation.surface: Commending the EU's record on good restraint of global crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking highly of someone in a tribute or encomium, as at a funeral.

clue.text: It is hard backing second-rate horse essentially in race

indicators.note: coming behind and supporting, so these pieces follow the others

parts.note: B, a B-grade, is second-rate

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter, so take the middle of horse

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A sentence about betting on a poor horse in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like betting on the horse but places the later pieces after the first two; 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Britain taken as a nation, a people or race.

clue.text: Inclined to cry, first of those facing reprimand

indicators.note: placed in front of, so the first letter comes before the scolding
take the opening letter of the word those

parts.note: an earful is a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: The first people to get a dressing-down are close to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the verge of weeping is near to tears.

clue.text: Inexpensiveness of gold daughter accepted in good humour

indicators.note: welcomed inside, so the metal and the daughter go into the good humour

parts.note: affability is friendliness and good nature
OR is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Wondering how cheap gold is, a daughter takes it cheerfully.
explanation.walkthrough: OR as gold comes from heraldry; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapness: the quality of being within one's means to buy.

clue.text: Dance with student also involved in tempestuous affair

indicators.note: mixed up within, so the learner and also go inside

parts.note: high as in high winds or high seas, stormy
a fling is a brief romantic affair
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A student caught up in a stormy romance dances with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: L for student comes from the learner plates on British cars driven by those learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively traditional Scottish solo dance, performed at Highland games.

clue.text: Love file sent with email message

definitions.meaning: a document added to and sent along with an email

explanation.surface: A love letter sent with a file attached to an email.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a bond of affection and a computer file accompanying an email.

clue.text: Though appearing gutless, steals pounds

indicators.note: with its insides gone, only the outer letters of though remain

parts.note: robs means steals from

explanation.surface: Someone seems spineless yet still takes money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' looks like sterling, but is the verb of beating heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb: beats or pulses strongly, as a headache does.

clue.text: Accommodation for sections of society

definitions.meaning: lodgings, as in soldiers' living space
districts of a city, such as a Latin or French area

explanation.surface: Housing provided for different social groups.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lodgings and divisions or districts of a town.

clue.text: Yard shut about when in the week?

indicators.note: moving around, so the letters of yard and shut are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks which weekday the yard closes.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week, the one after Wednesday.

clue.text: Arabs, in theory, will secrete potent drink

indicators.note: to secrete is to hide, so the words hold the answer concealed inside them

explanation.surface: Arabs, it is supposed, would hide a strong spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong green aniseed spirit flavoured with wormwood, once banned in France.

clue.text: Unusually generous fortune finally escaping theatre worker

indicators.note: not in the normal way, so the remaining letters are rearranged
getting away, so this letter leaves the word generous
the last letter of the word fortune

explanation.surface: A lucky windfall slips away from a generous stagehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping' removes E, the end of fortune, from GENEROUS; 'Unusually' shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who operates in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Those originally inside Rolls-Royce arriving at opera?

parts.note: a Rolls-Royce is a luxury car
men, the people who were riding in the vehicle

explanation.surface: The passengers of a Rolls-Royce get to the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arriving at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's popular opera about a Spanish gypsy; the question mark flags the playful wordplay.

clue.text: Rising Oregon tenor's opening line for skilled musician

indicators.note: in a down clue going upward means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: OR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Oregon

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word tenor's

parts.note: a seam is a stitched line joining fabric

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming Oregon tenor opens with a line for a virtuoso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses ORTSEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished conductor or master performer of music.

clue.text: Familiar with gripping, tense, uplifting poems you articulated

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is heard as the single letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the pronoun spoken aloud

indicators.note: holding tight, so the reversed poems hold the tense
in a down clue, lifting up means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: odes are lyric poems
T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar

explanation.surface: Gripping, uplifting poems you recite with tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns ODES into SEDO, and 'gripping' puts T inside it, all after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed to, as in being used to hard work.

clue.text: Place near London, order fish there mostly for distribution

indicators.note: dealing out and spreading, so the letters are redistributed in a new order
most of the word, with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Instructions to order fish from somewhere near London for delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'mostly' cuts THERE to THER; 'for distribution' shuffles ORDER, FISH and THER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Home County just north of the capital, with towns such as St Albans and Watford.

clue.text: Plant, one supported by stake briefly

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up by what sits below, so the next piece comes beneath

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a risk is a stake, as in a gamble

explanation.surface: A single plant held upright by a short garden stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens RISK to RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant with sword-shaped leaves, also called a flag.

clue.text: About to enter English court, Edmond's case is established

indicators.note: going in, so the word for about goes inside the other letters

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: the outer letters of a word form its case, like a shell round its contents

explanation.surface: About to go into an English court, Edmond's legal case is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal but takes the outer letters of Edmond.
explanation.definitionFit: Set up or built, as a monument is set up or raised.

clue.text: Over time medic provided gear periodically for vagrant

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming before, so the first pieces go ahead of the next

parts.note: DR is short for doctor
if means provided that

indicators.note: at regular intervals, taking every other letter of gear

explanation.surface: A doctor, over time, supplies equipment to a homeless wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' picks ER from gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who wanders aimlessly without a fixed home or job.

clue.text: Flipping insect bite

indicators.note: turning over, so the insect's name is read backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: An irritated reaction to a blasted insect bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild curse but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, pungent flavour or piquancy, as in a cheese with bite.

clue.text: Unknown's article replaced by vacuous story expressing same idea

indicators.note: swapped out for another piece, so the article gives way to the outer letters

parts.note: an unknown author is nameless, unnamed
A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: empty, so only the outer letters of story remain

explanation.surface: An unknown writer's article swapped for an empty tale says the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' empties story to SY, which replaces the first A of ANONYMOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the same meaning, as two equivalent words do.
